    Home/How we rate

    How we rate peptide products and sellers

    We judge every shop by five checks and every online clinic by four, and build every goal page by the same rule. The checks are facts we hold about a seller, not a safety grade.

    Peptide Chooser editorial team. Last updated 30 Oct 2026. Every claim links to its source. Prices checked 30 Oct 2026.

    The seller checks

    Online clinics prescribe and ship medicines; they publish no lab reports, so a clinic is checked on four facts, not five: no FDA warning letter, registered company, legal pages, fresh prices. A shop is checked on five. A score is never compared across the two kinds.

    Every shop page and every price window shows a line such as "3 of 5 checks", every clinic page "3 of 4 checks". These are the five, in the order the seller page shows them; a clinic has all but the first. We recompute them each time we pull our data, and the seller page shows the date as "Checked" and a date.

    Lab reports

    Met when the seller has published at least one lab report (a certificate of analysis) dated in the last 12 months, for any of its products. We read the reports on the seller's own pages. A miss means we found no report from the last 12 months; it does not mean a product failed a test. A lab report shows what one batch contained on the day it was tested, not that a product is safe or that it works.

    No FDA letter

    Met when the FDA's public list of warning letters holds no letter matched to the seller by its web address or street address. A letter that only shares a company name is not counted, because names repeat. A miss means the FDA sent the seller at least one warning letter; the seller page links each one.

    A warning letter is the FDA's notice of violations it believes it found. The company responds, and when the FDA has verified the corrections a close-out letter follows. A letter does not withdraw any approval. We show a seller's letter next to its price and every letter on its page, and a letter alone does not stop a paid link. We still refuse a paid link in two cases: a research-use shop, always, and a seller whose letter is about adulterated drug products while the FDA has published no close-out letter. What the FDA says about warning letters

    Found in a state registry

    Met when we find the business behind the shop in a state business registry, matched with high confidence. A miss means we did not find it. We do not search every state's registry yet, so a real company can still show as not found. When an FDA letter names the company, the seller page says so, but that alone does not meet this check.

    Legal pages

    Met when the seller's site has a terms page and a privacy or refund page, seen by our crawler in the last 30 days. A miss means we did not see those pages in that time. Having them says nothing about what they promise.

    Fresh prices

    Met when our own price crawl saw at least one price per milligram on the seller's site in the last 30 days. A miss means our prices for this seller are older than that, so read them with care.

    What the score does not tell you

    A seller with 5 of 5 can still sell a product that is not approved for any use. A seller with 0 of 5 is one where we found none of the five facts, not one where we found five problems; only a missed "No FDA letter" check means we found something against the seller. Read the checks one by one.

    How a goal page is built

    • When the FDA has approved a treatment for the goal, it is listed first.
    • Research-use peptides are shown with one sentence on their FDA status. We never link to a research-use seller: the price window lists the shops by name, and each name opens our page on that seller.
    • Online clinics get a white "See plans" button to our own page on the clinic until we have a paid link with that clinic. A paid link is a green button with "Paid link" under it.
    • Every price shows the date we checked it, and every claim links to its source.

    What does not change a check

    Paid links, partnership requests and a seller asking us. A seller with a paid link is checked the same way as one without, and no one can buy a higher score or a better place on a page.

    Corrections

    If you find an error, email hello@peptidechooser.com with the page and the source. We correct confirmed errors, note the date of the change and list it on our corrections page.
